chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from a man whom he named, said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who marries the woman for a single 'ard (visit/going to bed). He said: There is no problem, but when he is finished, let him turn his face away and not look.

key_terms.عَرْد: A period of time or a visit, often used in Mut'ah to denote the duration of the marriage contract.
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on temporary marriage for a single visit in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of a minimal duration in temporary marriage (Mut'ah), affirming that a contract for a single sexual act is valid. The instruction to 'turn his face' signifies the immediate termination of the contractual bond upon consummation, a key jurisprudential point distinguishing Mut'ah from permanent marriage. This highlights the flexibility of the 'ajl' (term) in Shia fiqh, where the duration can be as brief as the act itself.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from a man whom he named, said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who marries (Mut’a) the woman upon only going to bed once. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem, but when he is free, so let him turn his face around and not look’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Faddal from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from a man whom he mentioned who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who married a woman (in the manner of al-Mut‘ah (advantageous marriage)) for only once going to bed. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is permissible, however, when the specified time ends he must turn his face away and must not look.’”
